facts.material: shrimp (Penaeus vannamei, 44.45 percent) and vegetable filling in a rice flour wrapper
facts.form: individually formed, quick-frozen spring rolls, about 35 g each, in airtight retail trays of 20; requires cooking

gri_path: GRI 1: chapter 16 note 2: food preparations containing more than 20 percent by weight of crustaceans fall in chapter 16; shrimp at 44.45 percent exceeds 20 percent

Chapter 16 note 2 exception for stuffed products of heading 1902 considered: the rice-flour spring roll wrapper is treated as a wrapper, not pasta (following HQ H341768 on shrimp dumplings with a non-pasta dough jacket)
GRI 1: heading 1605 crustaceans, prepared or preserved
GRI 6: 1605.2 shrimps and prawns; packaged in airtight trays, so 1605.29 (other than not in airtight containers)
GRI 6: 1605.29.05.00 products containing fish meat; prepared meals

rejected_alternatives.reason: stuffed pasta, frozen; applies only if the rice-flour wrapper is pasta (as with the dim sum noodle rolls in N343875); a spring roll wrapper was treated as not pasta
for goods not in airtight containers; the rolls are packed in airtight trays
baked spring roll skins with vegetable filling (H305436); here shrimp exceeds 20 percent so chapter 16 note 2 applies

missing_facts: Is the rice flour wrapper made like pasta/noodle dough (which would make it stuffed pasta of 1902)?
Are the trays hermetically sealed airtight containers in the tariff sense?
classification.rationale: The spring rolls contain 44.45 percent shrimp, so chapter 16 note 2 places the preparation in chapter 16 unless it is a stuffed pasta of 1902. Following HQ H341768, which placed frozen shrimp dumplings with a non-pasta starch wrapper in 1605.21.05 as a prepared shrimp product, the rolls are classified in heading 1605. Because the description states they are packed in airtight retail trays, the airtight-container subheading 1605.29 applies, at the 'prepared meals' line 1605.29.05.00. If the wrapper counts as pasta, the answer would be 1902.20.00.40.
